sections.voiceover: Researchers at the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument used the Mayall 4-meter telescope at Kitt Peak National Observatory to track these stars. How did they calculate such a massive total?
sections.visual_cue: The Mayall 4-meter telescope dome at night.
b_roll: Mayall 4-meter telescope at Kitt Peak National Observatory

sections.voiceover: But the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument team used four complex motion-tracking techniques to calculate the total.
sections.visual_cue: Data visualization showing four overlapping model curves.

sections.voiceover: A separate study verified this using 279 blue-hot stars and 213 pulsating stars at extreme distances. The Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument survey team measured the Milky Way using these stellar samples.
sections.visual_cue: Animation highlighting star clusters at the edge of the galaxy.

sections.voiceover: Researchers use the Mayall 4-meter telescope at Kitt Peak National Observatory to map galactic mass.
sections.visual_cue: Slow zoom out from the galactic center to the dark void.
